territorial_scope.description: California statute amending the Government Code; applies to committees creating, publishing or distributing qualified political advertisements under that code.

evidence.quote: If a committee, as defined in Section 82013, creates, originally publishes, or originally distributes a qualified political advertisement

summary.short: Adds Government Code § 84514, requiring political committees that create, originally publish or distribute qualified political advertisements containing AI-generated or substantially altered media to carry a prescribed AI disclosure. The Commission may seek injunctive relief or other remedies; the excerpt states no start date.
summary.long: Adds Government Code § 84514. A committee (as defined in § 82013) that creates, originally publishes or originally distributes a qualified political advertisement must include, clearly and conspicuously, the disclosure “Ad generated or substantially altered using artificial intelligence,” displayed or spoken as prescribed in §§ 84504–84504.5 (as applicable). The section does not alter Section 230 rights or immunities of interactive service providers. If a committee does not comply, the Commission may seek injunctive relief under § 90009 or pursue administrative or civil remedies under Chapter 3 or Chapter 11; a violation is not a misdemeanor. Definitions cover “artificial intelligence”, media that is entirely AI-created and would falsely appear authentic or materially AI-altered so a reasonable person would have a fundamentally different understanding, and immaterial edits (cosmetic, colour, crop or resize) that are excluded. A “qualified political advertisement” is one containing such image, audio or video. The excerpt states no effective date.

The excerpt does not name the code for these references; read as Government Code because the new section is added there.

notes: Excerpt: Sec. 8 of AB 2355 only (partial extent). The registry title names the Political Reform Act of 1974; the excerpt does not name that Act. The term Commission is not defined in the excerpt. No internal inconsistencies found; subdivision (c)(2) states that a violation of (a) is not a misdemeanor, while (c)(1) gives the Commission civil and administrative options.

thresholds.note: The annotated provision (Gov. Code § 84514 as added by AB 2355, Sec. 8) contains no numeric cutoffs. Its scope turns on non-numeric definitions (qualified political advertisement, generated or substantially altered media) and on the committee definition by reference to § 82013. The only numbers are statutory section and chapter references, which are not thresholds.
